title: Akasa Air Extends Saudi Suspension to October 27, Longest of Indian Carriers
excerpt: The Indian Embassy in Riyadh's consolidated October 18 flight list puts Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo at October 24 on all routes and Akasa at October 27, with Saudia and Flynas Dammam services still flying to India.
body:
• Akasa Air has extended its suspension of all Saudi Arabia routes until October 27 — three days beyond Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo, which are grounded until October 24 on all routes, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said on Sunday.
  • Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport remains shut; Dammam, Jeddah and Medina airports are operating with some disruptions.
  • Flights home still exist: Saudia flies to India from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, and Flynas runs Dammam–Delhi and Dammam–Mumbai services from October 17 to 24 plus scheduled Dammam–Lucknow flights.
  • If you need to leave urgently, the embassy says you may transit via Bahrain, Kuwait or Qatar if you obtain the necessary visas; in an emergency in Saudi Arabia call 911 in Makkah, Madinah, Riyadh and the Eastern Province, or 998 elsewhere.

Akasa Air will not fly to or from Saudi Arabia until October 27, the longest suspension of any Indian carrier, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said in a consolidated flight update on Sunday. The extension pushes Akasa three days beyond the October 24 cutoff that now applies to Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo on all Saudi routes, and replaces Akasa's earlier split dates of October 24 for Riyadh and October 21 for Jeddah.

The embassy published the unified list in a fresh advisory on October 18, reported by IANS and summarised by Livemint. It is the first single statement setting out every Indian carrier's end date since the October 10 strike on King Khalid International Airport, which killed an Indian national, closed Riyadh's airport.

"The Indian Community in Saudi Arabia is advised to take due precautions under the prevailing situation. In case of an aerial attack, immediately proceed to the nearest safe place (inside a building or an interior room away from windows), and refrain from filming, publishing, or sharing any information, photos, or videos related to the ongoing events."

— Indian Embassy in Riyadh, advisory posted on X

One List, Four Different End Dates to Plan Around

Until Sunday, travellers had to piece together separate airline announcements. Air India and Air India Express confirmed on Saturday that they would stay grounded until October 24, with one free date change for travel up to November 10 — details in our coverage of that extension. IndiGo had already moved to October 24. Akasa's move to October 27 is the new fact, and it means there is still no single day on which India–Saudi flying fully resumes.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Hili9QW5foo

The embassy said flight operations remain shut at Riyadh's international airport, while Dammam, Jeddah and Medina remain operational although some disruptions continue, according to IANS. Anyone holding an Akasa booking for travel before October 28 should not head to the airport and should rebook or seek a refund through the airline instead.

The Flights That Are Still Operating

The same statement listed services still moving. Saudia is operating scheduled flights to India from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina. Flynas is operating Dammam–Delhi and Dammam–Mumbai flights between October 17 and 24, its scheduled Dammam–Lucknow services continue, and Flyadeal operated Dammam–Mumbai flights on October 17 and 18.

https://x.com/AkasaAir/status/2111766828275925346

For urgent departure, the embassy repeated that nationals may transit through Bahrain, Kuwait or Qatar, subject to obtaining the necessary entry visas. It warned Indians planning travel to Saudi Arabia, including Umrah pilgrims, to expect cancellations that could prolong a stay, and urged anyone with queries to contact its 24x7 control rooms.

Safety Guidance, in Brief

Sunday's flight update accompanied a renewed safety advisory telling nationals to move to an interior room away from windows during an aerial attack and refrain from filming the events. The fuller Saudi Civil Defense directives relayed the same day — stay off balconies and rooftops, and call 911 or 998 in an emergency — are in our earlier report on the October 18 safety directives.

Embassy officials continue to visit hospitals treating the Indians injured on October 10 and remain in touch with their families, the mission said. The Ministry of External Affairs said on Wednesday that of the 11 injured who survived, three had been discharged and eight remained in hospital, four in intensive care. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated India's condemnation of attacks on civilian infrastructure as "unacceptable," IANS reported.

What This Means for Indians in Saudi Arabia

Saudi Arabia hosts an estimated 2.4 to 2.7 million Indians. If your return is on an Indian carrier, treat October 24 as the earliest resumption for Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo and October 27 for Akasa — and if you cannot wait, book the Flynas Dammam–Delhi or Dammam–Mumbai services running through October 24 or a Saudia departure from Dammam, Jeddah or Medina rather than waiting for Riyadh to reopen.
